# Can we do better?

## The good: it stays a distribution

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}
```julia
using CensoredDistributions, Distributions, Turing

@model function delay_model(values, weights)
    α ~ truncated(Normal(1, 2), 0, Inf)
    θ ~ truncated(Normal(1, 2), 0, Inf)
    d = double_interval_censored(
        Gamma(α, θ); upper = 15, interval = 1
    )
    values ~ weight(d, weights)
end

chain = sample(delay_model(values, weights),
               NUTS(), MCMCThreads(), 1000, 2)
```
:::
::: {.column width="46%"}
- Each adjustment is a wrapper on a `Distributions.jl` object.
  `primary_censored` is the $w_P$ integral, `upper` truncates at $C$,
  `interval_censored` is $w_S$
- The stack is still a distribution, so Turing takes it as it is and
  the delay is built from the sampled parameters
- Multiple dispatch picks the closed form when the pair has one, and
  the numerical integral otherwise
- `cdf(primary_censored(Frechet(2, 1), Uniform(0, 1)), 3.0)` returns
  `0.847`. Nobody wrote that method. In Stan `Frechet` needs a branch,
  an integer and a rebuild

::: {.attribution}
Model from `CensoredDistributions.jl/README.md:67-81`, run for this
talk against v0.2.22 · fallback at
`src/censoring/primarycensored_cdf.jl:184-188` ·
[CensoredDistributions.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/CensoredDistributions.jl)
:::
:::
::::

## The bad: automatic differentiation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
```
# the Gamma closed form
MethodError: no method matching
  _gamma_inc(::Dual, ::Float64, ::Int64)

# and once a rule was written for it
Enzyme forward -> [-0.21736, -0.21296, 0.19054]
ForwardDiff    -> [-0.23692, -0.21296, 0.19054]
```
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- `SpecialFunctions` has no `_gamma_inc` method for a `Dual` shape, so
  our Gamma closed form would not differentiate
- Adaptive quadrature would not either. Its node count depends on the
  integrand, so the trace is a different shape each call
- Lifting a correct `ChainRulesCore` rule into Enzyme returned a wrong
  shape partial and two right ones, with no error

::: {.attribution}
[EpiAware/CensoredDistributions.jl#217](https://github.com/EpiAware/CensoredDistributions.jl/issues/217)
and
[#259](https://github.com/EpiAware/CensoredDistributions.jl/issues/259),
April and May 2026 · `src/integration/integration.jl:14-20`
:::
:::

## What the autodiff cost us

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
| Autodiff backend | Broken |
|---|---:|
| ForwardDiff | 0 |
| ReverseDiff, tape | 0 |
| Mooncake forward | 3 |
| Mooncake reverse | 3 |
| Enzyme forward | 4 |
| Enzyme reverse | 8 |

::: {.attribution}
Scenarios registered broken out of 63, in
`test/ADFixtures/src/ADFixtures.jl:177`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
- 2,724 lines of test infrastructure, 63 scenarios and a CI workflow
  per backend. `DifferentiationInterfaceTest` is what made any of it
  testable, and it is good
- 480 lines of hand-written rules across `gamma_ad.jl` and five
  autodiff extensions, for one Gamma CDF derivative
- The default solver is `GaussLegendre(; n = 64)`, because fixed nodes
  trace through every backend and adaptive ones do not. I got there by
  hacking around the integral in sad confusion
- I still cannot give a user a straight answer on which backend to
  pick
